description: Lossless package readback for exact demographic targeting. requested preserves canonical buyer intent; applied states the canonical predicate actually booked; execution identifies the seller mechanism. Sellers MUST book only when requested and applied denote exactly the same set, including unknown-age membership. Unsupported predicates are rejected; a buyer that chooses another supported predicate submits it as a new request. Buyers SHOULD recompute equality from the two predicates.

applied.description: Canonical demographic predicate actually applied by the seller.

age.description: A canonical audience-age predicate in completed integer years. min and max are inclusive; omitting one bound means no restriction in that direction. At least one bound is required. include_unknown is always explicit because people whose age is unavailable are not members of any numeric interval. Implementations MUST reject min greater than max; JSON Schema draft-07 cannot compare sibling numeric values.

max.description: Inclusive maximum age in completed years. Omit for an open upper bound.

min.description: Inclusive minimum age in completed years. Omit for an open lower bound.

age.title: Demographic Age Range

applied_bases.description: Effective user-level determination bases configured for this package after intersecting buyer accepted_bases, product supported_bases, and age_restriction. This is an auditable configuration readback, not proof that every impression used every listed basis.

applied_verification_methods.description: Effective verification methods when applied_bases contains verified. A method name does not establish that a particular proof or claim was valid; runtime verification and claim entailment remain required.

equivalent.description: Always true for a stored package. requested and applied MUST denote exactly the same set, including unknown-age membership; sellers reject non-equivalent requests instead of storing an alternative.

accepted_bases.description: User-level age determination bases the buyer permits for this predicate. Sellers MUST use only these bases or reject the request; they MUST NOT silently fall back to another basis.
